## Purpose and dependency

This is a **validation PR stacked on #172**. It targets `perf/video-recovery-eof-release-20261028-2d367` and adds **no production changes** relative to that implementation.

The research confirmed that the video session retains its final compressed recovery GOP after normal EOF until a later reset. The existing buffer admits up to 512 packets / 32 MiB of payload. While this experiment was running, parallel implementation PRs appeared; this work now independently qualifies #172's generation-checked release at the existing drain/EOS boundary.

## What this PR adds

- A reproducible comparison of the exact baseline/candidate session methods and each variant's complete packet-owner source, with real FFmpeg backing allocations.
- A final-release probe that transfers the original native reference and retains no extra observer reference.
- Debug/release CI against the repository's verified **FFmpeg 8.1.2** source archive.
- Three expanded actual-decoder ownership cases covering retained decoded pixels, an independent native packet clone, and cancelled-drain replay.
- A research report and permanent raw observations, complete controlled-output receipts, commands, and source/toolchain provenance.

## Measured result

The [qualified Linux job passed](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/actions/runs/40640946283/job/122658686684), using **Swift 6.4.1 / x86_64 Linux**.

| Synthetic final GOP | Baseline backing bytes at EOF | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 4 × 256 KiB packets | 1,048,832 | 0 |
| 512 × 64 KiB packets | 33,587,200 | 0 |
| 4 packets, one independently retained native buffer | 1,048,832 | 262,208 |

The independent consumer's remaining buffer stays readable and releases when that consumer closes. Counts are identical across both configurations and both fresh-process pair orders.

These are live native backing bytes, **including FFmpeg input padding**. They exclude packet/reference metadata, instrumentation and allocator overhead. The capacity workload does not establish typical media savings or whole-player RSS reduction.

## Validation

**Passed at `29227795552097be22675e0a8c498481042e44b3`:**

- 72 primary observations and 36 complete behavior comparisons across nine scenarios, debug/release, and AB/BA pairs.
- Normal/repeated EOF, partial-output failure, cancellation, stale EOF, independent ownership, empty input, and later-generation controls.
- Both baseline negative controls fail specifically with exit 73 and `EOF_RELEASE_REGRESSION`; both candidate controls pass.
- All allocations eventually free exactly once; complete controlled output sequences match.
- Independently audited raw evidence and source hashes. The candidate owner matches #172 at `c1ef6aff6060ad35decbc6dce0c224164be941a2`; the baseline owner comes from `ea2ff568237e2667f7b1aeee67b11a44ebe95b72`.

The final commit adds only the report and evidence; measured production, harness, and test inputs are unchanged.

**Pending:** [macOS component and native-regression jobs](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/actions/runs/40640946230) are queued. The full application/test build and new decoded-pixel tests are not claimed as executed. Keep this PR **draft** until native qualification succeeds.

The controlled-loop outputs are receipts, not decoded pixels. Visible UI, hardware playback, scheduler concurrency, and whole-process footprint remain separate scopes. The release follows the existing normal-return drain contract, preserving replay on thrown errors and cancellation.

## Review and reproduce

[Measured results, rationale, and limits](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/blob/5af8eea6ddd786765f2aea4ad10bbb42085c5360/Benchmarks/VideoRecoveryEOFMemory/RESULTS.md) · [Reproduction instructions](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/blob/5af8eea6ddd786765f2aea4ad10bbb42085c5360/Benchmarks/VideoRecoveryEOFMemory/README.md) · [Raw evidence](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/tree/5af8eea6ddd786765f2aea4ad10bbb42085c5360/Benchmarks/VideoRecoveryEOFMemory/evidence/linux)

After #172 merges, rebase/retarget this validation PR onto main as appropriate. Hosted builds explicitly record Kyoto's absence and run serially in isolated checkouts; reproduction uses Kyoto where available.
